symptom: The same .mpr passed as `App.mpr`, `./App.mpr`, an absolute path or with `\` read the catalog cache as 'Invalid (MPR path changed)'; queries then ran on a narrower catalog built in memory and returned plausible but wrong results (CATALOG.ACTIVITIES empty, GRAPH_DEAD_ASSETS inflated).
cause: isCacheValid compared the stored -p text with the current text byte for byte. The cache sits at <dir of the .mpr>/.mxcli/catalog.db, so any spelling that finds it names the right folder; the text compare was only meant to catch a second .mpr there. cmd_describe's catalogMatchesProject had a second copy that resolved a relative stored path against the cwd.
fix: catalog.SameMprPath: a relative stored spelling is resolved in the current .mpr's folder, then os.SameFile (cleaned absolute paths, case-insensitive on Windows, when either cannot be stat'ed). Both checks use it; new caches record the absolute path (AbsMprPath).
insight: A cache keyed on user input text is keyed on the spelling, not the thing. Prefer the identity the cache's own location already guarantees, and os.SameFile for the rest. The second half of the report — an invalid cache serving a narrower in-memory build as if complete — is the fast-consumer design in ensureCatalog and is not changed here.
test: mdl/executor/catalog_path_spelling_2200_test.go TestCatalogCache_AnySpellingOfTheSameMprIsValid (control: another .mpr in the same folder is invalid)
